utterances.text: Well, we didn't, not that day when they set the ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When did you hand over your weapons?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: Several weeks before the attack on Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So -- does the Defence have any questions? My colleague would like to ask the question, then I'll give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, you have seen a photograph of Stupni Do, and you have made a cross where your location was. Would you be able, if you were shown that photograph again, to draw the different trenches that had been dug for the defence of Stupni Do? Would you remember? Could you do that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would then -- then I would ask the usher to present you again with that picture and a pen. It is this one, I think. Take this. Mm-hmm. That's not the one. The one where the witness marked a cross. He put a cross. Yes. This is the one, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. There's another photograph where you can see the entire village. That might be more appropriate to indicate where the trenches were. So please show this photograph to the witness. That might be -- might speak for itself. So please put the photograph on the ELMO so that everybody can see it, my photograph. So that said, we have an overall view here, an aerial view. Now, can you mark the areas where the trenches were with a cross.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: I can only mark two trenches. The others can't be seen. On this photograph, you can only see two of them. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can we have a number, please, for these two trenches.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit IC 777.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now we will ask the witness to mark the other trenches on the other photograph. You can only see two trenches on this one. So here we have it. This is the first photograph, and you had marked a cross on this one. So can you tell us where the trenches were?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: Bogos hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please indicate where the trenches were.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: This is the trench. There were just two trenches there, and it was called Do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't tell us where the other trenches were? You can't mark those?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: I can't because they're not on this picture. If you have another photograph, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have an exhibit number for this map also, please, registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number IC 778.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, among all those photographs you've seen, is there one on which you could mark all the trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Among the photographs that the Prosecution has shown you, is there one of these photographs which would enable you to locate all the trenches, all the trenches that were dug around the village, because so far you've only showed us two. You don't understand my question?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: I will show them when you show me another photograph. I saw Bradvica and Borava Glava a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Flynn, during your examination, that is what you should do. You should have remembered to ask him to locate trenches on the photographs and to mark these.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes, but I was short of time and I was trying to be expeditious. I can't ask all the questions, Your Honour. Perhaps -- I mean, if you wish for a clarification, when I showed these photographs to him yesterday he was able to mark more than two, and maybe if you would like to show him the very first photograph again, I think he might be able to mark a number of the trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we'll show you again the two photographs. Please take a look at this one. Can you indicate other trenches on this one?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do so then.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number for that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number IC 779.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a bit surprised when I see you marking those trenches. Why aren't there any trenches in the lower part of the photograph? It seems that all the trenches are on the line which is north on that photograph, but are there any other trenches in the east, in the west, in the south?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC
utterances.text: There were just trenches, seven of them, on all sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there were seven trenches on all sides. Okay. Fine. Did we give a number to the last photograph? Very well. Mr. Ibrisimovic, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were supposed to start off with the cross-examination, but our Defence team does not have any questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence doesn't have any questions or you don't have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for the Pusic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prlic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prlic Defence likewise has no questions, and we cede our time to the other Defence teams if they need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, not for Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just have one question, and my client would like to ask two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, don't limit me in that way. Don't limit me. These are very technical questions, clear questions, and there's no point in not approaching the truth of Stupni Do, whatever that truth might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise I thought there were changes. As I said I have one question:

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Could you take up the photographs you were looking at a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. If there's one question from Mr. Kovacic, two questions from Mr. Praljak, and if there's no more questions from other Defence counsel we might be able to finish today, otherwise, everybody will have to come back tomorrow. Ms. Alaburic, will have you questions to ask to that witness or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. The Petkovic Defence does have a few questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that there's been a misunderstanding. I misspoke, but General Praljak intervened. He hasn't only got two questions, he has more. Not many, but quite a bit more, which we won't be able to get through in the next five minutes certainly. So it's up to you, of course. We shall abide by your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. If Mr. Praljak Defence needs five minutes, if Ms. Alaburic has a few questions to ask, a few minutes, maybe, and if there is no question from Mr. Coric, maybe we could finish by 7.15. Right. So we will finish by 7.15. It's better for us to finish with that witness rather than to have him come back tomorrow for a few minutes. Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, I really do think that this is an important part of the indictment and an important witness, because he was a member of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian army and he can speak about the combat activities that were undertaken in the village and the preparations for the village of defence of a possible HVO attack. I don't think it would be right to reduce the cross-examination to just some 10 minutes. So I would like to propose that we leave the cross-examination of this witness for tomorrow even if it only lasts half an hour, to do it in the proper way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you wish. Sir, your hearing will continue tomorrow since the Defence so wishes. We'll meet again tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of January, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
